extraction.summary: The paper tests two phenomenological Everpresent Λ implementations against Pantheon+SH0ES supernova data and Planck CMB likelihoods, then separately constrains flexible background-only dark-energy histories around and away from recombination. Model 1 uses stochastic Λ increments scaled by the growth of an observer's past-light-cone four-volume; Model 2 uses a bounded tanh transform of a correlated Gaussian process. In the authors' finite seed samples (with unresolved posterior-weighting descriptions), a small subset of Model 1 histories gives competitive Pantheon+SH0ES fits and those selected histories tend to have smaller, less matter-tracking low-redshift fluctuations. The paper's Model 1 CMB fits are substantially worse than ΛCDM under the stated implementation; suppressing Λ at last scattering improves the best likelihood but leaves it worse than ΛCDM. Flexible spline histories admit small late- and pre-recombination deviations and some improved best-fit CMB likelihoods, but these are parameterized background histories, not a derived Everpresent Λ model. The paper explicitly lacks a developed quantum-gravity dynamics for Everpresent Λ and discards histories with H²<0.

ideas.title: Model 1 scales stochastic Λ increments with past-light-cone four-volume
ideas.description: The phenomenological Model 1 takes Λ to have zero-mean Gaussian fluctuations whose scale decreases as the observer's past-light-cone four-volume grows. At each step the Friedmann background uses separately redshifting matter and radiation plus ρΛ=Λ/(8πG). The paper treats this as a phenomenological realization motivated by causal-set/unimodular ideas, not as a derived quantum-gravity evolution law. It starts at a finite radiation-era four-volume; histories for which H² becomes negative are discarded because replacement dynamics are unknown.

ideas.title: Model 2 maps a correlated Gaussian process to bounded ΩΛ
ideas.description: The phenomenological Model 2 sets ΩΛ(λ)=tanh[ΩhatΛ(λ)], with λ=log(a), where ΩhatΛ is a mean-zero Gaussian process with squared-exponential covariance. This bounds ΩΛ to (-1,1); the paper says μ=O(1) approximately reproduces basic Model 1 features. Its later CMB chains do not converge in the authors' trials when α̃ becomes very small and μ loses relevance.

equations.conventions: ΩhatΛ is a mean-zero continuous Gaussian process.
α̃ and μ are free parameters.

ideas.title: Competitive supernova fits occur in a rare, selected seed subset
ideas.description: For the 90,000-seed fixed-seed SN analysis, the authors report 55 seeds with best-fit χ² in [1481,1490] and 16 with likelihood better than their ΛCDM reference χ²≈1485.3. Their best-fit seed has χ²=1481.9, H0=72.18 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Ω_m^0=0.33, and α=0.0092. The paper reports posterior summaries as model averages (weighting implementation unresolved) of H0=73.27±1.27 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Ω_m^0=0.58±0.19, and α=0.0085±0.0017. The selected good-seed curves have smaller low-z Λ fluctuations and do not track matter as closely as poor-fit examples. The authors report correlation between mean Om over z∈[0.1,0.8] and χ², but the paper prints an internally impossible threshold for one subset (see caveats). These are finite-sample fit results, not a general probability that the model beats ΛCDM.
locators: PDF p. 11, Figure 4 and accompanying paragraph

ideas.title: Model 1 CMB fits are poor under the stated perturbation and scaling prescription
ideas.description: For a 100,000-seed search, the authors prefilter to 3,106 seeds using their H0 and Ω_m,min criteria; 91 then have Planck likelihood statistic below 3000. The best Model 1 value is -2 log L≈2495.6 versus ≈2339.0 for ΛCDM (Δ≈156.6). Across qualifying histories the fitted H0 values are about 40-51 km s^-1 Mpc^-1; 82/91 chains spend most of their time at Ω_m h²≈0.16-0.20, although the best chain has Ω_m h²=0.1408. Multiplying ρΛ by a Gaussian-like suppression around z=1100 with Δz=100 or 200 raises the accepted counts to 248 or 539 and reduces the best -2 log L to 2360.5 or 2358.5, still worse than ΛCDM. Model 2 trials also fail to produce competitive H0/fits, but their implementation is not comparable to ref. [1] because this paper permits the full sign and magnitude range while that earlier analysis used a narrow negative w(z) range.

equations.conventions: Ω_r^0 is held fixed from the CMB temperature while Ω_m^0 is varied.

ideas.title: Spline background histories permit small CMB-compatible deviations in selected epochs
ideas.description: Separately from the stochastic Everpresent Λ realizations, the authors fit a five-node spline f(z) to background dark-energy density histories, fixing f and its derivatives to zero at the epoch boundaries. After recombination, nodes are z={1,10,50,100,500}, radiation is neglected, and the best -2ΔlogL is 5.68. Before recombination, nodes are z={2140,4570,10000,21380,45710}, radiation-scaled contributions are added, and the best -2ΔlogL is 9.02; the authors report mean dark-energy fractions 0.6±0.6% at z≈5000 and 1.0±1.5% at z≈20000, consistent with zero within 1σ. They report the latter histories raise h and change their historical Hubble-tension estimate from 5σ to 3.5σ. The chosen node locations affect detailed feature positions; the likelihood is multimodal, and the mean history need not itself fit well. This parameterization is not a derived Everpresent Λ physical model.
locators: PDF p. 25, Figure 13, Eq. (6.16), and Table 2

caveats.claim: The Model 1 CMB result is conditional on turning off dark-energy perturbations. The authors explicitly say Model 1 dark energy is not a fluid. The paper supplies no alternative stress-energy/perturbation closure for this stochastic component, so the poor likelihood is not a general CMB falsification of a completed Everpresent Λ theory.

For CMB tractability the authors precompute histories on an α grid and rescale/interpolate them. Their proportionality with Ω_m h² is approximate across radiation- and matter-dominated eras and fails at equality; they scale the eras separately, say the equality interval is small in conformal time, and report a numerical check that it does not change Cℓ. The equality implementation and check are not independently auditable from the article.

The SN and CMB results condition on finite fixed-seed sets; the seed lists and sampling errors are unavailable. Main text Eqs.(4.3)-(4.4) weights normalized fixed-seed posteriors by P(s|D) proportional to marginal likelihood times seed prior; harmonic-mean likelihood estimates are stated. Appendix A Method 3 Eq.(A.6) instead says average normalized posteriors equally. Those operations differ unless seed evidences are equal. Actual implementation is unknown; preserve source-reported Eq.(4.5) as a conditional reported result, not independently verified model marginalization. CMB preselection adds another conditioning step; counts and best-fit extrema are not global model evidence.

The optimized best SN seed is not model evidence. The main-text weighting uses per-seed marginal likelihoods, while Appendix A describes equal normalized-posterior averaging; implementation is unknown. Harmonic-mean estimates are source-reported without estimator or seed-pool sensitivity validation.

The reported H0 posterior is fit using the Pantheon+SH0ES sample including 42 calibrators and is compared to SH0ES H0. That comparison shares the local calibration lineage and must not be treated as independent confirmation. The authors also note that the model-independent SH0ES Taylor expansion assumes smooth H(z), which they say is not generally appropriate for a stochastic history.

Section 4.2 states that 70 seeds have χ²<1060 while reporting ⟨Om⟩=0.27±0.03. This is incompatible with the section's best SN fit χ²=1481.9 and the Figure 4 χ² axis, which is around 1500-8000. The printed PDF and extracted text both read 1060. I did not silently change it to a conjectured value.

No conflict: Appendix B explicitly defines Hcal=aH (PDF p.31). B.13 uses Hcal, Eq.(6.9) uses cosmic H. Thus sigma≈z_star/(10^4 Hcal_star)=z_star(1+z_star)/(10^4 H_star)≈z_star^2/(10^4 H_star) at z_star>>1. Preserve the approximation and distinguish conformal time from cosmic time.

Sec.4.1 states 55/90000 in [1481,1490] and 16/90000 better than LambdaCDM. Arithmetic fractions are about 0.0611% and 0.0178%. Sec.7 says about 0.14% similar and 0.015% better. The similar-fit threshold is not restated there, so this is an unreconciled summary, not proof the same precisely defined subset was miscounted. Use exact Sec.4.1 counts with finite-sample conditioning; do not turn summary percentages into model probabilities.

The LSS suppression is an artificial modification motivated by prior work, not a derived correction to Model 1. The free f(z) MCMC analyses are flexible background parameterizations, not Everpresent Λ realizations or a complete physical dark-energy model.

The f(z) conclusions depend on five selected interpolation redshifts and boundary conditions. The authors report node-dependent feature positions, a high rejection rate, and multiple likelihood minima; the plotted mean history need not be a good fit.

For the free-f(z) analyses the paper explains background parametrization and use of SCoPE but does not state a sufficiently explicit perturbation closure for the modified component to reproduce its treatment independently. Exact code, seed, likelihood, and data identities are also absent.

Model 1 diverges or is undefined at t=0 and is initialized instead with a nonzero radiation-era volume. Histories that reach H²<0 are discarded; their correct dynamics are unknown. The authors explicitly say their phenomenological model does not describe the quantum-gravity initial epoch.

usefulness.assessment: Useful source for a bounded, assumption-aware investigation of what low-redshift shapes and CMB epochs constrain; not a completed model qualification or independent reproduction.
usefulness.strongest_reason_for_bounded_investigati: The paper gives a concrete candidate discriminator for competitive Model 1 SN histories—smaller, weakly matter-tracking fluctuations at z≲1.5 and lower ⟨Om⟩—and shows that CMB likelihood changes sharply with the behavior around last scattering and with small, epoch-local background variations. Those are specific claims that can be checked against exact seeds and code.
usefulness.strongest_objection: The central Model 1 CMB null is inseparable from the authors' decision to turn off dark-energy perturbations, which is not a validated closure for a physical Everpresent Λ component; the approximate equality scaling and unpublished seed/code artifacts add further uncertainty.
usefulness.cheapest_nonduplicative_next_test: First obtain/pin the exact modified CAMB/CMBAns source, likelihood identity, and one published best-fit seed/history. Then do one paired calculation for that seed: compare the article's interpolated/piecewise equality scaling with a direct background integration through equality and inspect ΔCℓ and the same Planck likelihood. This isolates the claimed harmlessness of the approximation without repeating the 100,000-seed scan; it would still not settle the missing dark-energy perturbation closure. Those artifacts are not supplied here, and no calculation was run.
usefulness.qualification: Full Luna reading only. No Sol review, independent reproduction, current-data reassessment, or scientific qualification has occurred.
